classification.difficultyReason: Recognise an equilateral triangle in the two-circle arrangement, combine a same-arc angle and common-chord perpendicular relation, then obtain the chord using a bisected base and Pythagoras.

content.prompt:
Let two circles of radius $1$ and centres O and P each pass through the centre of the other, and intersect at F and G.

Let FG meet OP at M.

spec.description: Two equal overlapping circles with centres O on the left and P on the right. Their upper intersection is F and lower intersection is G. Common chord FG crosses OP at M. Segments OF, OG, PF and PG are drawn, together with FG and OP.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens/point identities retained, no computed student values or added proof segments.

answer.worked: OF=PF=OP=1, so triangle OFP is equilateral and $\angle FPO=60^\circ$. In the circle with centre P, the circumference angle FGO stands on the same arc FO as central angle FPO, so $\angle FGO=30^\circ$. The interval joining the centres is perpendicular to their common chord, so $\angle FMO=90^\circ$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the length of the common chord FG.

answer.worked: Since OF=PF, the perpendicular FM bisects OP, so $OM=\frac{1}{2}$. In right triangle OMF, $FM=\sqrt{1^2-(\frac{1}{2})^2}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. The perpendicular from centre O bisects chord FG, so $FG=2FM=\sqrt3$.
